issues.legal_issue: A fresh land-acquisition declaration made within the applicable statutory period is not invalid solely because it followed the initial notice after a long delay.
material_facts: An initial notice proposing acquisition was issued before the 1967 amendment took effect.

The first declaration was invalidated because the acquisition benefited a corporation, no part of the compensation was to come from public revenue, and the requirements for acquisition for a company had not been followed.

After the invalidation, the government gave the affected landholders an opportunity to make further objections and a personal hearing, then issued a fresh declaration within two years of the amendment’s commencement.
The fresh declaration was challenged only on the ground that it came more than fifteen years after the initial notice.
issues.conclusion: The fresh declaration was valid and could not be struck down solely for unreasonable or unexplained delay because it was made within the statutory period applicable to notices issued before the amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4(2) and 6(1), including the proviso added by the Land Acquisition (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1967, establish time limits for making a declaration: for an initial notice issued before the Ordinance commenced, the declaration must be made within two years of commencement; for a notice issued after commencement, it must be made within three years of publication. Where the legislature prescribes a period for exercising a power, exercise within that period cannot be invalidated solely as unreasonably delayed. The earlier inter partes decision in Valjibhai Muljibhai Soneji v. State of Bombay invalidated the original declaration because the acquisition benefited a corporation without public revenue contributing to compensation and the requirements of Part VII had not been complied with.

predicates.land_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns a challenge to a government declaration made in a land-acquisition process.
predicates.initial_notice_pre_amendment: The initial notice proposing the acquisition was issued before the relevant statutory amendment took effect.
predicates.fresh_declaration_within_transition_peri: The government made the fresh declaration within the transitional period applicable to an initial notice issued before the amendment.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition challenge concerns an initial notice issued before the amendment and the fresh declaration is made within the applicable transitional period, the declaration is not invalid solely for delay.

issues.legal_issue: When a party joined as the karta of a continuing Hindu undivided family dies during an appeal, the succeeding karta may be substituted under the procedure for substitution of a deceased party, and the substitution may suffice despite use of an incorrect procedure.
material_facts: A respondent joined in the appeals as the karta of a joint Hindu family business died while the appeals were pending.

The family continued to exist, and its succeeding karta was brought on record through applications made under the procedure for devolution of interest rather than the procedure for substitution of a deceased party.
The applications appeared to have been made after the limitation period, but the succeeding karta was already on record when the objection was considered.
issues.conclusion: The applications under the procedure for devolution of interest were not the correct procedure; an application for substitution under Order XXII Rule 4 should have been made. However, because the succeeding karta had been brought on record, the court overruled the objection.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXII Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, where a party joined as karta dies and the undivided Hindu family continues, the succeeding karta can be substituted for the deceased karta. An application under Order XXII Rule 10 is not the correct procedure for that substitution, but the court may overrule a technical objection where the succeeding karta has already been brought on record.

predicates.appeal_involving_karta_party: The proceeding is an appeal in which a party was joined in the capacity of karta of an undivided Hindu family.
predicates.family_continued_after_karta_death: The undivided Hindu family continued to exist after the karta died during the appeal.
predicates.successor_karta_brought_on_record: The succeeding karta was brought on record in place of the deceased karta, although the application used was not the correct procedure for substitution.

issues.definition: When an appeal involves a deceased karta, the family continues, and the successor karta is brought on record, the substitution may suffice and an objection based on the procedural error is overruled.
